articles.title: Lisandro Martinez: Argentine media’s verdict on United ace after 7-0 Burkina Faso win
articles.summary: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez had a fruitful outing for Argentina in the 7-0 win over Burkina Faso in a friendly on Saturday, 3 October, at th...
articles.body:
Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez had a fruitful outing for Argentina in the 7-0 win over Burkina Faso in a friendly on Saturday, 3 October, at the Estadio Mâs Monumental. The Butcher was called up to the national team for the international friendlies and also featured in the 4-0 win over Bolivia earlier this month.

Martinez is enjoying a decent year so far, after playing a key role in the Red Devils' rise under Michael Carrick in the second half of last season. The Argentine was a regular feature under Michael Carrick as he switched to a back four from former head coach Ruben Amorim's 3-4-3 system.

Martinez added defensive solidity alongside Harry Maguire and helped the English giants finish third in the Premier League, subsequently securing their participation in this season's Champions League. Over the summer, the 28-year-old helped Argentina reach the final of the 2026 FIFA World Cup, starting every game bar one.

Unfortunately, Licha picked up an injury in the final as La Albiceleste were defeated 1-0 by Spain. Nevertheless, the Argentine returned in time to briefly feature for United in pre-season and has been heavily involved this campaign so far.

Martinez started the campaign on the bench, as an unused substitute in the 2-0 defeat at the hands of Hull City on opening day. He has subsequently played every minute of every game in the Premier League.

The Argentine scored his first Champions League goal in the 4-0 win over Sabah last month.

However, Martinez has also come under scrutiny this season, especially with United currently struggling in the Premier League, where they sit 12th in the table after five games. The Red Devils have conceded eight goals in the league so far and are yet to register a clean sheet.

Nevertheless, Licha had a comfortable outing against Burkina Faso on Saturday, although the fact that the opponents had to name a weakened side due to off-field issues certainly helped. The United star registered a 97% pass completion rate, while completing two of his three attempted long balls, before he was substituted at the break.

His performance has now been appreciated by the Argentine media.

TyC Sports gave Martinez a rating of 6 out of 10, noting: "Like Cuti (Romero), he came off at half-time. He didn't have any major problems either."

La Pagina Millonaria , meanwhile, pointed out that Licha was precise in his passes, also handing him a 6/10 rating. The report stated: "Much the same as Cuti, although he was under less defensive pressure than the captain. His touches came whilst building play from the back and, like his partner, he was precise. He was substituted at half-time."

El Destape Web , however, was far more impressed, giving him a 7 out of 10, adding: "He was once again solid in defence and was hardly called upon at the back. He played for just one half."

The United star also earned a 6/10 rating from La Voz , who stated: "Another player who was on the pitch long enough to add another win to his record, but he didn't face any difficulties."

Martinez's contract expires in less than a year, so the coming weeks could be crucial for his future at United. With Maguire also out of contract next summer, the Red Devils may have to consider a defensive upheaval in 2027.

articles.title: New Liverpool star raising serious £47m dilemma
articles.summary: Ronald Araujo Gives Liverpool a Different Edge as £47m Question Starts to BuildLiverpool have spent the opening weeks of the new season searching for certain...
articles.body:
Ronald Araujo Gives Liverpool a Different Edge as £47m Question Starts to Build

Liverpool have spent the opening weeks of the new season searching for certainty after a campaign in which too much felt improvised, especially in defence. According to ECHO , one of the more unexpected answers has come in the shape of Ronald Araujo, a player borrowed from Barcelona and asked to solve a problem that has tripped up plenty of others.

It is a fascinating subplot because it says plenty about where Liverpool are, what Andoni Iraola values, and why the club may soon have a serious decision to make over a reported £47m option. Araujo did not arrive as a glamorous headline signing. He arrived with a touch of uncertainty, some baggage from a difficult spell in Spain, and the sense that he might be useful across the back line. What has happened since is more interesting than that. He has quickly become an important part of Liverpool's unbeaten start, and he has done so by playing a role that is not naturally his.

There is a certain irony in that. Liverpool have spent a long time grappling with the after-effects of life after Trent Alexander-Arnold, whose gifts were so singular that replacing him like-for-like was always going to be impossible. Since his departure to Real Madrid in 2025, the club have tried a variety of answers. Some were practical, some were desperate, and some simply exposed how awkward the question had become. Injuries, patchwork selections and short-term fixes all played their part in destabilising the side.

Araujo has not tried to imitate what came before. That may be why this has worked. He offers a defence-first interpretation of the role, one built on concentration, strength, timing and the kind of authority that eases anxiety in those around him. It changes the geometry of Liverpool's back four. It gives Virgil van Dijk a trusted ally beside him and allows the line to defend space with greater conviction. Clean sheets have followed, and confidence tends to travel quickly once defenders start to believe the ground beneath them is stable again.

Right-back role reshaped under Andoni Iraola

That shift matters because Iraola is still imposing his ideas on this team. Early in a new era, a manager will take reliability over romance every time, and Araujo has provided that. He may see himself as a centre-back, and in the long term Liverpool may still imagine him there, but his current job has clear value. He has made the position more secure, more combative and more sensible. In a side still learning its new manager's demands, that has real importance.

The backdrop to all this is Conor Bradley's absence. Liverpool still appear to view Bradley as the long-term fit for the position once he is fully recovered and back to full sharpness. His energy and aggression suit the role, and there is a feeling inside the club that his athletic profile can give Liverpool balance without asking him to mimic the passing repertoire of Alexander-Arnold. But for now that remains a plan for later, not a solution for today.

Today belongs to Araujo. His impact has been noticed by those around him and Van Dijk's verdict carried weight. "He is a great player," said the Liverpool captain. "I don't think he was the captain of Barcelona for no reason.

"He is a fantastic player. He is not a natural right-back but he has filled in the best way possible and I am pleased for him. It has been an intense couple of weeks for him.

"So hopefully now in this international break, he can get a little bit of rest before the chaos will start when we come back. It is down to the whole team, but obviously he did very well so far."

Those comments underline something else Liverpool have needed, leadership. The departures of senior figures in recent windows have left the squad a little lighter in personality and voice. Van Dijk remains the obvious standard-bearer and Alisson Becker continues to lead in his own measured style, but dressing rooms thrive on a spread of authority. Araujo arrived with that reputation already formed. He had captained Barcelona, he carries standing with Uruguay, and at 27 he has enough experience to command respect without saying too much.

£47m transfer decision growing on Merseyside

So the £47m question looms. It is far too soon to declare it an obvious bargain or an unavoidable priority. Liverpool will want a longer sample, Bradley's recovery will influence the thinking, and Araujo's own adaptability across the season will matter. Yet this much is already clear, the conversation has changed. What looked like cover now looks like possibility. What felt temporary now carries the first hints of permanence.

That is the mark of a successful start. Araujo has not arrived with noise or theatre. He has simply done the hard parts well, defended properly, brought calm to a troubled area and reminded Liverpool that solutions in football do not always come wrapped in glamour. Sometimes they arrive in a borrowed shirt, playing slightly out of position, and asking a club to think harder about the future than it expected.

From a Liverpool supporter's point of view, this report is intriguing because Araujo seems to offer something the squad has badly needed, authority. Not every fix has to be spectacular. Sometimes you just want someone in that back line who looks like he enjoys defending, relishes duels and gives everyone else a lift.

The key thing here is that he appears to complement what Iraola is trying to build. Liverpool looked far too open at times last season and there were matches where the right-back slot felt like a warning light on a dashboard. If Araujo can steady that side while Bradley gets properly fit, that is already valuable.

The £47m figure still feels significant, and supporters will want to see more before calling for a permanent deal. There is a difference between a strong start and a full-season answer. Even so, there is enough here to believe this may become one of those smart pieces of business that grows on everyone very quickly.

What makes it especially interesting is the leadership element. Liverpool have lost important voices over the last year or two, and teams chasing major honours need more than talent. They need personality. If Araujo keeps defending like this and keeps adding that edge to the dressing room, plenty of fans will start wondering whether £47m is actually the right price for a problem solved.

articles.title: Report: Italian giants eye Brighton star to replace legend
articles.summary: Milan Eye Yasin Ayari Transfer as Brighton Midfielder Gains €40m ValuationAC Milan are planning ahead, and Yasin Ayari has clearly entered the conversation....
articles.body:
Milan Eye Yasin Ayari Transfer as Brighton Midfielder Gains €40m Valuation

AC Milan are planning ahead, and Yasin Ayari has clearly entered the conversation. According to Football Italia , the Brighton midfielder is being tracked as a possible answer to future changes in Ruben Amorim's midfield, where age, form and contract uncertainty could soon force a reset.

The logic is straightforward. Luka Modric is 41 and into the final year of his deal. Even if he keeps going, Milan are unlikely to keep stretching that situation indefinitely. Ruben Loftus-Cheek has an unclear future, Ardon Jashari has yet to convince fully, and the broader midfield picture may look very different by the end of the 2026-27 campaign.

Ayari fits the profile of a modern midfield target, mobile, technically clean and increasingly influential. Brighton have used him heavily under Fabian Hurzeler and he has responded well. His early-season goal in the 5-0 win over Coventry City underlined that progress, and Italian scouts have clearly taken note long before that.

Reports suggest Milan's interest goes back to early 2025, when Geoffrey Moncada was still technical director. That matters. Clubs do not keep revisiting the same player unless there is broad internal agreement on his level and his potential.

The reported €40m valuation is substantial, though hardly outrageous in the current market for Premier League-developed midfielders. Ayari is also in the final year of his Brighton contract, due to expire on June 30, 2027, though the club hold an option to extend by another 12 months. That weakens any idea that Brighton are under immediate pressure.

From Milan's side, this feels like sensible groundwork rather than a deal close to completion. They know midfield succession planning cannot be left until the last minute. From Brighton's side, this is the cost of developing good players well. If Ayari keeps performing, interest will grow and the number attached to his name will remain high.

As a concerned Brighton supporter, this report is annoying because it follows a familiar pattern. A player develops, starts the season well, and within minutes someone abroad is circling. Ayari has not just filled a shirt, he has looked like a midfielder with authority, composure and the ability to shift games. Brighton should be thinking about building around that, not preparing for the next sales pitch.

The contract detail matters most here. If the club really have an option for another year, then they must use that position properly. There is no reason to act like a selling club in a panic. €40m sounds impressive on paper, but replacing a midfielder who knows the system, is still improving and already contributes in the Premier League is rarely simple. Usually it costs more than expected, takes longer than expected, and weakens the team in the meantime.

Supporters will accept interest from Milan because that is what happens when players perform. They will not accept softness. Brighton need to be strong, either extend Ayari on better terms or make it clear that any move would require a massive fee. Otherwise it becomes another story where Brighton do the smart recruitment, the coaching and the development, and somebody else tries to cash in on the finished product.

articles.title: Spain hold off Czechia to move within one point of quarter-finals
articles.summary: Spain beat Czechia 3-1 in Oviedo on Saturday 3 October, with Lamine Yamal scoring inside six minutes for a third consecutive game. The victory kept Spain’s N...
articles.body:
Spain beat Czechia 3-1 in Oviedo on Saturday 3 October, with Lamine Yamal scoring inside six minutes for a third consecutive game. The victory kept Spain's Nations League campaign perfect and left them one point from the quarter-finals, according to the Guardian's match report.

Spain built a two-goal lead before the break

Yamal had gone close inside the opening minute, but his goal arrived after five minutes and 20 seconds. Dani Olmo exchanged a quick one-two with the Barcelona teenager, who collected the ball near the top-right corner of the area and curled a shot into the far corner.

The pattern was becoming striking: Yamal had scored after 104 seconds against England and 70 seconds against Croatia. In Oviedo, he made it three goals across those three matches in 494 seconds. He was withdrawn at half-time, with Spain already 2-0 ahead.

Rodri had doubled the lead in the 32nd minute. The midfielder advanced from near the centre circle, played the ball to Pedri and received it back after a defender's touch before driving his shot high into the net. Spain had 13 shots to Czechia's one by the interval and 70% possession.

Rodri with teammates Pau Cubarsí and Unai Simón.

Czechia threatened before Merino settled it

The match looked under control, but Czechia improved after the break. Jiri Slama pulled a goal back in the 69th minute, steering Adam Hlozek's pass beyond Spain goalkeeper David Raya after a move built from deep.

Czechia thought they had equalised when Ryan Naderi turned in the rebound from a header, but referee Vassilis Fotias had already stopped play. The Guardian reported that Fotias judged there had been a foul on Robin Le Normand during the free-kick that led to the chance. Czechia were reduced to 10 men soon afterwards, and Mikel Merino scored with two minutes remaining to secure the result.

The late pressure made the final score less comfortable than Spain's first-half control suggested. Raya had also misplaced a pass that presented Ondrej Lingr with a chance, while Lingr later missed an opportunity to score into an unguarded goal.

Spain remain a point from the quarter-finals

The win maintained Spain's perfect start in the Nations League group and put them within touching distance of qualification for the quarter-finals. Yamal's latest early strike was the headline, but the match also offered a reminder that Spain's control can be tested when opponents raise their intensity after the interval.

Luis de la Fuente, Spain's manager, said Yamal was on course to become a legend. The assessment followed another decisive contribution from the Barcelona forward, whose goals have helped Spain make a rapid start to the campaign.

articles.title: Cologne suffer double striker injury blow ahead of crucial Bundesliga derby
articles.summary: Cologne have suffered a significant double injury blow after both Thijs Dallinga and Ragnar Ache were forced off during Saturday’s international-break friend...
articles.body:
Cologne have suffered a significant double injury blow after both Thijs Dallinga and Ragnar Ache were forced off during Saturday's international-break friendly against Viktoria Köln.

The most serious concern surrounds Dallinga. Cologne confirmed on Saturday evening that the 26-year-old suffered a cruciate-ligament injury and will consequently be sidelined for several months. Ache, meanwhile, sustained a muscular injury in his thigh and will also be unavailable for the time being.

The circumstances made an already difficult afternoon particularly cruel. Dallinga initially required treatment after hurting his knee during a penalty-area situation and ultimately had to be helped from the pitch. Ache replaced him in the 35th minute.

Approximately ten minutes later, Cologne's other established centre-forward was also struggling. Ache remained in the dressing room at halftime after suffering his own injury, meaning the cathedral city side effectively lost both of their primary strikers within the space of ten minutes.

Dallinga's promising Cologne start interrupted

Dallinga only arrived in the Bundesliga ahead of this season on loan from Bologna. His start could scarcely have been more encouraging. Dallinga scored twice on his league debut against Hoffenheim after coming off the bench.

The weeks that followed proved more difficult. Dallinga missed a penalty in the 1-1 draw with Werder Bremen and failed to convert another excellent opportunity in the defeat to Hamburg.

The Dutchman had nevertheless already established himself as a legitimate competitor for Ache's starting position. There also remained the possibility of head coach René Wagner using both centre-forwards together.

That option has now disappeared for the foreseeable future.

Ache's injury compounds the problem considerably. The 28-year-old played an important role for Cologne throughout last season and developed into one of the club's most dependable attacking weapons after initially requiring time to settle at Bundesliga level.

The timing is particularly unwelcome. Cologne return from the international break with an October 11 derby against Borussia Mönchengladbach before facing Eintracht Frankfurt and promoted Schalke in the Bundesliga. A DFB-Pokal meeting with Union Berlin also follows later in the month.

Marius Bülter appears the most obvious candidate to fill the vacancy in the short term. The 33-year-old scored Cologne's equalizer in Saturday's 2-2 draw with Viktoria and possesses extensive Bundesliga experience playing both centrally and from wider positions. Wagner may nevertheless have to reconsider his attacking structure altogether while awaiting further clarity on Ache's recovery.

Dallinga's absence will regrettably be measured in months.

articles.title: Greg Schiano faces 'tough decisions' at Rutgers football's bye week
articles.summary: Rutgers football is 1-4 and coach Greg Schiano vowed to examine just about everything during the team's upcoming bye week.
articles.body:
PISCATAWAY – Rutgers football is heading into a bye week , and coach Greg Schiano vowed to examine just about everything.

He needs to, because his team continues to struggle.

The Scarlet Knights lost 47-15 to defending champion Indiana on Saturday, falling to 1-4 as the disappointing and frustrating start to the season continues, largely because of a defense that has failed to play to the level it needs to in order to be competitive.

"We didn't perform well enough," Schiano said. "That's taking no credit away from Indiana, they've won 21 straight. They're a heck of a football team. Well coached, good players. But I expected us to play better. It's my job to get this fixed. I've been doing this a long time, I know how to do it. I've got to go do it. I can't talk about it, got to do it."

Travis Johansen's unit gave up 593 total yards of offense. The Hoosiers rushed for 329 yards. They averaged 8.7 yards per play.

Too often, players on Rutgers' defense were out of position.

The Hoosiers connected on too many explosive plays, something Schiano earlier in the week his team needed to limit.

Schiano said he saw improvement the previous two weeks – a seven-point loss to USC and a blowout win over FCS-level Howard – but that disappeared against Indiana.

"I do think we have to examine exactly what we're doing in all phases of defense and what are we capable of doing here and now," Schiano said. "Not maybe a year from now or two years from now, but what are we capable of doing effectively (now)."

The unit underwent a complete overhaul in the offseason after also struggling last season.

A new coaching staff, more than 10 new transfers.

None of it has worked, starting from the stunning and embarrassing season-opening loss to UMass.

Pictures from college football national champion Indiana vs. Rutgers

Schiano said he'd look at everything, but stopped short at saying exactly where he'd begin or what it might involve.

"Anything's on the table – like I said, I love the coaching staff, I love the players," Schiano said. "It won't be any of that. It's going to be what can we do improve? We have to improve. I thought we did improve the last weeks and we didn't improve this week."

Schiano said he still has full belief in his coaching staff to fix the problem.

"It's like anything, why do you believe anything? Because I do," Schiano said. "That's a choice. Belief in something is a choice. I believe in these guys because I've worked with them every day and I see the players practice. I know how we're capable of improving."

Schiano said his team needs time to improve.

The Scarlet Knights will have a week off to find some answers.

It better find them, or else the final seven games could be as ugly as the first five.

"Do I think we're make the College Football Playoff this year? No, I don't think we're there yet," Schiano said. "But again to me the operative word is yet. I think we will get there. It's frustrating right now, no doubt. There's a lot of reasons we are where we are. I know what we've got to do. Some of it just keep working. We need some time. Some of it is we better fix some things and change some things because it's not working. Belief is a strong thing if it's real."

articles.title: Newcastle 4 PSG 1 happened exactly three years ago, what a night
articles.summary: Yes, exactly three years ago today, Newcastle 4 PSG 1. The haters may say, ‘well so what, Newcastle United ended up knocked out in their group.
articles.body:
Yes, exactly three years ago today, Newcastle 4 PSG 1.

The haters may say, 'well so what, Newcastle United ended up knocked out in their group.'

However, that is missing the point entirely AND surely only people who never go to any matches ever, to see any team play, would say that.

You live for the moment and that moment three years ago today was Newcastle 4 PSG 1.

Ask anybody who was there inside St James' Park on 4 October 2023 if it was all meaningless in the end?

If you have the attitude that the only matches anybody can treasure, are ones that eventually lead to winning a trophy, then what would be the point of 99.999999% of football matches and indeed football clubs?!!

A small detail is that PSG have now dominated Europe the last three years, losing in the semi-finals and then winning the Champions League twice.

Anyway, we have reproduced the match report below from that Newcastle 4 PSG 1 game.

Also, we have included the video highlights of the match.

Newcastle 4 PSG 1 – The match report from Jamie Smith on The Mag back on 5 October 2023, the day after THAT night:

Right, tonight was the night, it's finally arrived.

The Champions League returning to St James' Park was something I thought I'd never see, or at the very least not for another generation. It was thinking of the next generation that prompted me to go against the usual instinct and sign my nine year old son up for these evening kick offs, I couldn't let him miss out on the days Tyneside had been waiting for.

Off the bus into town and the place was mental.

The police had the street at a standstill as PSG Ultras were marching up Blackett Street towards the ground, with hundreds of welcoming Mags greeting them with songs from a swathe of black and white.

Me and the boy squeezed past and grabbed a quick Nandos followed by a few settlers for me ahead of joining the throng for the journey up to the temple on the hill.

Everything just felt special. People were buzzing, random songs were sprouting up and all sorts of cameras kicking about outside. Inside the stadium was, of course spectacular. The ground seemed full to the brim a good half an hour before kick off and the flag display was reminiscent of the league cup final as everyone played their part turning the place black and white.

The noise was up to the level reserved for special nights as the repertoire included the ones set up by the DJ (spinning Hey Jude and Rockin all over the world to prompt the colloquial versions of both) and the more off the cuff, organically occurring tunes. It was brilliant and still managed to find an extra decibel as the teams emerged to line up, with the sound only decreasing slightly to give due reverence to the magnificent sound of the Champions League theme ringing out here for the first time in twenty years and seven months. If you don't count the Sam Fender gig.

My hope was that this would count for something. Of the sides in group F, PSG were probably the least used to huge intimidating atmospheres playing in the relatively moderate setting of Ligue 1. They were the most likely to freeze on our patch, wondering just where the hell they were and what the thump they'd gotten themselves into. The fact le Parisiens were the top seed and arguably the strongest opponent, meant we really needed to turn this situation to our advantage.

The game started in a similar way to our recent couple of league games as we survived a very avoidable scare, having presented the opponent with too much freedom at the back post. Instead of McAtee crossing for Thomas at Sheff Utd, or Koleosho breaking free for Burnley, this was World Cup final hat-trick scorer Kylian Mbappe steaming down on goal and knocking it to Ousmane Dembele at the back post. Dan Burn haring across seemed to do enough to put Dembele off and he drove his shot wide to the left of the goal. Early let off, so now we survive the first ten minutes with less possession, then settle down and control the game. You know what reader? That's exactly what happened.

Our first goal was one of the lushest, most magnificent moments ever and it's a shame it can only really happen once. PSG were starting to look ragged at the back under our high press and Marquinhos attempted a terrible weak ball out from the back that was seized on by Tonali, who controlled his header straight back in towards Isak. Isak turned into the ball and unleashed a vicious shot that Donnarumma got down well to save, but the power meant he could only send it back out towards the marauding Almiron, who provided the most sumptuously cool finish, powering it perfectly into the opposite corner. The sound was incredible, our first Champions League goal since Shearer in Milan. Screaming, hollering, even the odd wobbly lip. Big beaming smile from my little un as I chucked him up a height. This was almost a release, letting go of years of frustration and I still don't think we can all quite believe it.

To make things even better, United were now comfortably in the driving seat. Trippier tried a clever quick corner which Schar smashed first time but sent narrowly wide. Hmm, maybe Fab's in that sort of mood tonight. PSG were struggling to get out of their half as Bruno and Tonali had assumed complete control of the midfield, intercepting, hustling and generally just taking the ball off them, the best game these two have had together as they were everywhere.

With half time approaching a Trippier free kick created chaos in the box. Lascelles' header may have got an awkward deflection as Donnarumma desperately palmed the ball away, then had to get down t9 block Bruno's cheeky follow up attempt from a narrow angle. The ball only broke back to Bruno who floated it to the back post, with the goalie recovering yet again to claw Burn's header away. The ball was then cleared, a flag went up and my head was spinning about what exactly was happening. Then we realised play was stopped and the VAR check was up.

After what seemed like an age, the ref drew a little box and pointed to the centre circle. Dan Burn had scored for Newcastle, in the Champions League, against PSG. How this prospect would have sounded to him five years ago is mind boggling. Having seen it back, the most baffling aspect is how long it took to give this perfectly good goal as the goal line technology advised the ref it had passed and it was blatant that Marquinhos was playing Bruno onside where the alleged offence had been given, 2-0 man, this is mint.

We survived until half time despite a glut of injury time following an alarmingly long period on the deck for Isak, who emerged in some kind of Rab C Nesbitt outfit but blessedly apparently unharmed when it had seemed so much worse.

The second half opened to a tinge of nerves, things would need to be kept tight for a bit against top class opposition with a ballon d'or contender up front.

Or we could just plough into a 3-0 lead?

It took five minutes before Trippier picked Longstaff's run into the box. I think everyone expected him to look to square to Isak or Gordon in the middle, including Donnarumma apparently as he was taken entirely by surprise when Lobby hammered the ball under him and into the Gallowgate net. Two Geordies scoring in the same Champions League game, not even Shearer and Shola managed that. There was a sense that this may have provided a killer touch and we may have been able to enjoy the rest of the match with calm and confidence.

Course, PSG had to score five minutes later and set the nerves jangling, 17 year old Warren Zaire-Emery is a name that will definitely be heard again in years to come and having arguably been the visitors' stand out player it was of course him that created the goal, that spoilt a clean sheet record of over 500 minutes stretching back over a month. Zaire-Emery dinked a smart little ball over the entire defence that fooled everyone and allowed the onrushing Lucas Hernandez to glance a header past Pope. We almost got rescued by the VAR but this time the check didn't fall our way and rightly so as t'were a run timed to perfection. The Parisian fans celebrated with flares to accompany the incessant drum sounds up in level 7, they were determined to enjoy this and fair play to them.

A short period of nervousness followed, with the excellent Lascelles tracking Dembele's run and crowding him out. PSG showed a bit more urgency but Eddie utilised game management, replacing flagging players with fresh legs. I thought Tonali was outstanding, so was a bit surprised to see him go first for Anderson. Murphy followed for Almiron, whose non-stop running and probing earned him the man of the match award. Well deserved, although I would probably have given it to Bruno, looking back to his impervious best.

A nervy last ten minutes was navigated in spite of Pope slamming every goal kick directly out of play, before the game was sealed in the first minute of injury time. Schar won the ball with a strong tackle in midfield and, perhaps sensing the result was safe, decided to take it for a walk forward. He played a one-two with Murphy, receiving the ball back in his favourite position, ready to smash one from the edge of the box. Blam, top corner, 4-1, top of the group. Place went utterly nuts.

At this point my lad was jumping up and down on his seat, waving his scarf. This was a smart recovery from his dozing on my knee at half time and having a bit of a crash midway through the second. Adjusting to middle school with a few extra sports classes and the additional efforts required for his performances with Westerhope United U10 Silvers was all taking its toll a bit and I'd wondered if he had this late night in him.

To see him deliriously jumping around after Fab's goal made it all worthwhile and I know he'll love it in future to be able to say he was there.

He's not the only one, as I think every person here tonight appreciated what they had experienced thoroughly. Some day we'll maybe expect to coast through group games and maybe this will be a time looked back on fondly as we find our way in Europe's Premier Competition. There'll be a few characters sit up and take notice of us after tonight I can assure you of that.

Next CL games bring a double header with Dortmund that could prove definitive. I'd put us as favourites at home and if we can produce a performance close to this we could well take a commanding position to Germany against an opponent whose prospects will be looking bleak.

Hopefully we'll have a more complete squad by then, as the niggles will start to dissipate. Not so sure about West Ham though, as the suspended Gordon will be added to the absentees and there has to be concern over the kicking Isak took tonight. Eddie's squad has a way of reproducing the goods whoever turns out though, and a win in London would seal a truly remarkable run between international breaks, with a very good chance to recalibrate to keep what could well be a stellar season on track.

Regardless of what happens, we were provided with another timeless memory tonight. Incredibly, three players who were on various stages of the scrap heap under Steve Bruce took centre stage in tearing apart one of Europe's most ominous sides. Yes we've reinforced heavily around them but Schar, Longstaff and Almiron were a credit to the work of our manager tonight, as was every player in black and white.

Eddie's Euro conquering Mags man, how far can they actually go?

Newcastle 4 PSG 1 – Wednesday 4 October 8pm

articles.body:
The international break is almost over, with Barcelona set to resume their campaign next weekend as they take on Getafe.

It is a game where team selection could be crucial given that the majority of Barcelona players will be returning from a gruelling and lengthened break.

Many players, therefore, will have accumulated fatigue during this period, meaning Flick might have to make some key changes to his eleven.

Adeyemi will be fresh enough to start vs Getafe. (Photo by Lars Baron/Getty Images)

According to Diario SPORT , Karim Adeyemi option for Barcelona for their upcoming game against Getafe next weekend.

The German has returned from international duty relatively fresh , having been spared Germany's final two UEFA Nations League matches.

New coach Jurgen Klopp used the window as a testing ground, calling up as many as 44 players and splitting them into two groups.

That means the winger will report back to training on Monday rested and in good spirits, having impressed on his return to the national team following his controversial World Cup snub under previous coach Julian Nagelsmann.

Adeyemi featured for 155 minutes across two games and was among Germany's standout performers, earning the clear confidence of Klopp .

His fine international form mirrors a promising start to life at Barcelona, where he has already contributed three goals and two assists while alternating between starts and substitute appearances.

Gordon will likely be rested vs Getafe. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images)

Adeyemi's freshness could prove particularly useful given the workload of some of his teammates.

The German primarily competes with Anthony Gordon for the left-wing spot, and the Englishman is set to return far more fatigued.

Gordon, who has been in sensational form , scored again against Croatia and still has a fourth game to play against the Czech Republic, having featured heavily for England throughout the break.

That extra wear and tear could open the door for Adeyemi to come into Flick's plans against Getafe.

With three goals in three games for England and the full backing of Thomas Tuchel, Gordon remains a key figure, but managing his minutes will be important over a demanding run of fixtures.

For Flick, having two in-form, confident wingers to rotate is a welcome luxury. Adeyemi's rest, combined with his growing importance for Germany, makes him a strong contender to feature prominently when Barcelona return to action/

Liverpool and Atletico Madrid are keeping tabs on the situation of Barcelona midfielder Marc Bernal.

The teenager is set to assess his future should his minutes not increase under Hansi Flick, having been a substitute in four of his seven La Liga appearances this season. He's provided two assists in 292 league minutes.

Bernal made nine league starts last season and made his senior debut for Spain in the summer. However, the arrival of Rodri from Manchester City has increased competition for a first-team place.

Barcelona do not want to sell the 19-year-old, but the stance could chance should Bernal express interest in an exit and a suitable offer arrives. According to transfer journalist Juan Jesus , Atletico Madrid and Liverpool are front of the queue should Bernal decide on an exit.

Liverpool are in the market for a midfielder after the sale of Curtis Jones to Inter Milan in the summer. Jones departed for the San Siro in search of more minutes, with Liverpool failing to sign a direct replacement.

Ryan Gravenberch has also struggled to recapture his best form under new head coach Andoni Iraola, with another option being considered ahead of the January window.

articles.title: Santi Guardia: cuando juegas por una casa para tus papás
articles.standfirst: El centrocampista de los ‘millonarios’ deja una respuesta que habla claro de cómo se vive el fútbol en las inferiores argentinas
articles.summary: El centrocampista de los ‘millonarios’ deja una respuesta que habla claro de cómo se vive el fútbol en las inferiores argentinas
articles.body: “Mi ilusión sería comprar una casa para mis papás”, la respuesta de Santi Guardia, jugador de River de apenas 12 años y que juega como los ángeles en LaLiga FC Futures de Orlando, dejó a la reportera de Dazn, Elena G. Durán, tambaleándose. Las anteriores respuestas de los pequeños jugadores de otros equipos españoles como Real Madrid, Barcelona o Atlético iban más encaminadas a éxitos deportivos: “ganar una Champions”, “jugar en Primera”, “Meter un gol en una final con mi equipo”, y temas más ‘mundanos’. Pero la respuesta del chico argentino de River fue tan potente que aclaró muchas cosas que se vieron sobre los terrenos de juego en este y en otros torneos. La intensidad con la que pelean los argentinos en estas categorías está por encima de la del resto. Muy por encima. Quizá no sean los mejores táctica o técnicamente, pero a la hora del esfuerzo, del derroche físico y el desgaste, no hay nadie como ellos. Incluso hay ocasiones que superan los límites y en algún torneo les han tenido que llamar al orden. Compiten como fieras y en esa respuesta de Santino está la clave. Desde muy pequeños, el fútbol es mucho en Argentina. En las calles, pero también en los clubes. Es un diversión, un deporte... pero también una salida en muchas ocasiones a una situación vital más que complicada. Lo hemos visto miles de veces en jugadores profesionales que han llegado a la albiceleste. Salidos de barrios muy humildes y cuyos primeros sueldos sirvieron para aliviar la situación de sus familias. Cuando lo recuerdan, se echan a llorar por la emoción y el sufrimiento vivido. Quizá no sea el caso de Santino Guardia, pero el mero hecho de que su ilusión fuera “comprar una casa para mis papás”, ya define un fútbol diferente. En la fase de grupos River derrotó 2-0 a Orlando, que en el arranque había ganado con suficiencia a Palmeiras mostrando un equipo muy hecho. Después, batió por 3-1 al equipo brasileño. El oficio de River no se compra, no se puede entrenar y los argentinos vienen con él de serie. Un gusto.

articles.summary: River Plate ganó a Flamengo (2-1) y el Betis se deshizo del Atlético de Madrid (2-1)
articles.body: Real Betis y River Plate. La gran final de LaLiga FC Futures Internacional de Orlando está servida. El equipo verdiblanco se deshizo del Atlético de Madrid por un ajustado 2-1 aunque realmente dominó el partido con bastante suficiencia y tuvo muchas ocasiones para aumentar la diferencia. El segundo finalista será River Plate. Los argentinos han mostrado un poder competitivo enorme durante todo el torneo y se deshicieron de un 'juguetón' Flamengo por 2-1 aguantando el último apretón de los brasileños que no pudieron darle la vuelta al marcador. En lo referente a la final de consolación serán Sevilla y Palmeiras los que se disputen el trofeo tras no poder avanzar en el cuadro principal. La FC Futures Internacional disputa su décima edición en Orlando, ciudad de fantasía por excelencia en los estados Unidos y en un recinto especial. La 'burbuja' (complejo ESPN Wide World of Sports, en Walt Disney World Resort) se abre de nuevo para que catorce de las mejores canteras del mundo pongan a prueba su nivel e intenten cargarse al sorprendente Elche que es el invitado de honor de esta décima edición al proclamarse campeón de la FC Futures de Villarreal derrotando a los grandes de LaLiga en un torneo perfecto. Por LaLiga FC Futures han pasado, siendo niños, Pau Cubarsí, Lamine Yamal o Gavi y otras leyendas históricas como Xavi Hernández, Iker Casillas, Andrés Iniesta, Fernando Torres, Gerard Piqué, Cesc Fàbregas y Santi Cazorla. Ese vínculo entre formación y élite es, precisamente, lo que LALIGA lleva más de una década exportando con este torneo. Para los clubes españoles supone medir su trabajo de cantera ante rivales de primer nivel internacional; para el aficionado estadounidense, una oportunidad poco habitual de ver de cerca cómo se forma un futbolista en España.

articles.summary: La vuelta a un gol que no celebraba desde el Mundial acerca a la Araña a su propósito y el del Atlético de empezar a redimirse de su culebrón veraniego a la vuelta del parón
articles.body: cierto es que fue en mitad del paseo de Argentina ante una débil Burkina Faso, pero su necesidad iba mucho más allá de tratarse de un amistoso o de que el rival se presentara con jugadores sub 23. No pasará a la historia, pero para Julián Alvarez y el Atlético su gol sí tiene mucho significado. Pura inyección anímica en el propósito común de que la Araña inicie a la vuelta del parón la redención que permita dejar en un mal sueño su culebrón veraniego. "En el Atlético de Madrid necesitan que Julián esté de buena manera, nunca va a defraudar porque hace goles", señalaba Scaloni después de que la Araña volviera a celebrar una diana que no lograba desde los cuartos del Mundial frente a Suiza el pasado 12 de julio, después de que hubiera verbalizado ante los medios el deseo de salir al Barcelona que ya había trasladado a los dirigentes del Atlético al término de la temporada. De hecho, aunque fueron sus palabras las que lo han alejado de su afición, en el club rojiblanco nunca tuvieron duda de que donde sí sabe hablar es en el campo, por eso cerrado su caso con la continuidad, urge recuperarlo. Simeone, en su primera comparecencia tras estallar el culebrón, fue el primero en tenderle la mano. "La situación es muy clara, la entidad tomó una decisión que Miguel Ángel ha explicado muy bien. Nosotros desde lo deportivo estamos muy contentos con tener un futbolista como Julián y seguramente desde lo deportivo lo ayudaremos para que siga creciendo, para que siga mejorando y para que siga dando lo mejor que nos ha dado en estos últimos dos años, que fue un montón", afirmó desde Seúl. Más adelante, incluso después de que el Metropolitano expresara su sentir a Julián con una sonora pitada en su primera aparición frente al Villarreal, sería el vestuario, con sus líderes a la cabeza, el que 'perdonaría' el desliz de Julián. "Jugadores y capitanes hemos gestionado lo de Julián como un tema que ha pasado, él está con nosotros, lo estamos apoyando, está dando el máximo, ya ha jugado algún partido y ha dado todo lo que ha podido. Estoy seguro que hasta que esté aquí va dar el cien por cien de sí mismo y va a hacer todo lo mejor que pueda por este club y para traer los mejores resultados posibles", apuntaría Oblak. “Estamos muy cansados y sobre todo él. Al chico hay que dejarlo, que juegue, disfrute y que haga su trabajo, que es jugar al fútbol”, insistiría Koke. Un refuerzo de los capitanes culminado por otra de las voces más autorizas, un Cuti Romero que por su amistad con la Araña y por su liderazgo, se antojaba como otra pieza esencial para crear el mejor clima para que el delantero recapacitara, dejara atrás la mala gestión de su futuro durante el verano, recuperara la sonrisa y la moral y para que tratara de restablecer la normalidad y su relación con la grada de la única manera posible: con hechos sobre el verde. "A Juli lo veo muy bien, sacando todo lo que se creó y se habló de puertas hacia fuera. En la intimidad, que soy amigo y lo conozco desde hace mucho tiempo, lo veo con muchas ganas, con las mismas ganas de siempre, es una gran profesional", señalaría justo antes del derbi. Por eso el gol de Julián Alvarez no se trata de uno más, sino que era el que le permitía volver a recuperar las sensaciones de siempre. No importaba el rival (en el anterior amistoso frente al Bolivia se le había resistido pese a disputar todo el partido), sino volver a marcar, a empezar el despegue tras unos meses muy complicados. De hecho, no sólo culminaría una gran jugada colectiva, sino que antes ya había puesto el centro que Diallo se introduciría en su propia puerta, redondeando una participación de 45 minutos convertida en toda una gran inyección de moral. Un gran paso, en definitiva, que sucedió a su buen partido en Liverpool en el que acabaría lesionado y, sobre todo, en un derbi en el que si bien volvió a ser recibido con música de viento, acabaría recibiendo algunos aplausos tras rozar el gol o protagonizar alguna acción defensiva que evidenciaba que su incansable trabajo para el equipo nunca va a faltar. Brotes verdes que sitúan a Julián en el mejor escenario para empezar a ser de nuevo el delantero con el que aspirar a títulos a la vuelta del parón.

articles.standfirst: El equipo no fue capaz de ganar el curso pasado cuando la competición se detuvo
articles.summary: El equipo no fue capaz de ganar el curso pasado cuando la competición se detuvo
articles.body: LaLiga EA Sports afronta sus últimos días de parón. La competición calienta motores después de un largo paréntesis por los compromisos de las selecciones. El Sevilla ha trabajado desde entonces sin seis internacionales -Odysseas, Suazo, Kochorashvili, Sangante, Robbie Ure y Fran González, aunque el meta leonés regresó antes de la concentración con la sub 21 por unas molestias. Se recuperó y fue titular en el XV Trofeo Antonio Puerta. El Sevilla afrontará su primer compromiso, la visita al Levante, el próximo 12 de octubre a las 21.00 horas. Los de García Plaza afrontarán dos salidas consecutivas. Tras el duelo frente al cuadro granota, a los nervionenses les espera el Bernabéu el día 18 a la misma hora. El conjunto hispalense se marchó al parón quinto con 13 puntos tras un notable inicio del curso. El técnico recupera a Kike Salas y a Rubén Vargas. Más dudas presenta Stassin, que sigue sin trabajar con sus compañeros. El equipo blanquirrojo ha demostrado en el último torneo que mantiene la intensidad competitiva y el técnico ha podido calibrar el nivel de los jugadores que han tenido menos protagonismo en los primeros meses de competición. Va a necesitar a todos ahora que la Copa del Rey también se prepara para hacer su aparición. Pero al Sevilla no se le dan bien los parones. Al menos el curso pasado. Los andaluces perdieron en todos los partidos que disputaron después de que la competición se detuviera salvo en una ocasión, la primera, en la que empató en el Sánchez-Pizjuán (2-2 ante el Elche). En los siguientes partidos tras el receso internacional pinchó frente al Mallorca (1-3), el Espanyol (2-1) y el Levante (0-3) en el primer encuentro de este 2026. La dinámica no cambió incluso con el relevo en los banquillos. García Plaza se estrenó con el Sevilla tras el último parón de la temporada y el equipo perdió por la mínima con el entonces colista, el Oviedo.

articles.title: Al-Thani no responde por su hijo Rakan
articles.standfirst: 21 días de silencio por parte del jeque
articles.summary: 21 días de silencio por parte del jeque
articles.body: La detención de Rakan Al-Thani en Alemania no ha provocado, por ahora, la reacción que muchos esperaban. Han pasado 21 días desde que el hijo del jeque fue arrestado en Múnich, en una información adelantada en exclusiva por Radio MARCA Málaga, y su padre continúa sin realizar ningún movimiento público relacionado con el caso. Rakan está a la espera de ser trasladado a Málaga durante los próximos días. Su llegada supondrá un nuevo escenario para una causa que lleva años abierta, ya que será entonces cuando la justicia española pueda comunicarle directamente los delitos que se le atribuyen. Sin embargo, la situación no ha servido para sacar al jeque de su silencio. La detención había generado expectación en el entorno del caso. La posibilidad de que uno de sus hijos quedase a disposición de las autoridades alemanas hacía pensar que la familia podría reaccionar y que los abogados tomarían alguna iniciativa. Nada de eso ha ocurrido hasta ahora. Los expertos consultados por Radio MARCA Málaga también apuntaban en esa dirección. Fernández Mochón esperaba que el arresto provocase un cambio de escenario. “Tengo la ilusión de que esto va a mover el avispero, estoy convencido”, señaló. El abogado añadía: “No vería lógico abandonar a mi propio hijo, aunque conociendo al jeque…”. Y era contundente sobre la necesidad de una respuesta por parte del máximo accionista del Málaga: “Este señor debe reaccionar”. Paco Valverde incidía en la misma cuestión. A su juicio, la familia debería asumir la dimensión del problema y tratar de encontrar una solución después de tantos años de conflicto. “Si el padre fuera consciente de la situación, debería acelerar el proceso, ya que no llega a ninguna parte. No comprendo la actitud de la familia”, explicaba. El calendario avanza y Rakan Al-Thani está a las puertas de Málaga. Su extradición permitirá a la justicia española avanzar en un procedimiento que permanece enquistado desde hace años. Mientras tanto, el jeque mantiene una posición de absoluto silencio. En el entorno judicial relacionado con el Málaga CF se empieza a percibir cierta decepción por la falta de reacción de Al-Thani después de la detención de su hijo. Se esperaba algún tipo de movimiento que, de momento, no se ha producido. La próxima escena puede llegar con el aterrizaje de Rakan en España. Su llegada volverá a poner el apellido Al-Thani en el centro de la actualidad malaguista y puede generar una importante repercusión en redes sociales. Queda por saber si esta vez ese ruido será suficiente para provocar la reacción que no ha llegado tras tres semanas de silencio.

articles.title: Luka Modric 'ashamed' of Croatia's 'catastrophic night' against England
articles.summary: Croatia captain Luka Modric says he was "ashamed" of his side's performance on a "catastrophic night" against England.
articles.body:
Croatia captain Luka Modric said he felt "ashamed" of his side's performance in Saturday's 7-0 defeat at home to England in the Nations League.

It was the first time in 20 years as an international that the AC Milan midfielder said he had felt such emotion, describing it as a "catastrophic night".

Modric, 41, was making his 205th appearance for his country after recently agreeing to extend his international career under returning manager Slaven Bilic.

"You can't play football like that... we looked like we had four or five players less," said the former Real Madrid player, who helped Croatia to second-place and third-place finishes at the 2018 and 2022 World Cups during a storied career.

"It is difficult to find an explanation for such a performance without duels, fouls, aggressiveness, togetherness.

"I've been here for 20 years, but for the first time I feel ashamed after a game."

Croatia kicked off Bilic's second spell in charge with a 2-1 Nations League win away to the Czech Republic that put them above England in Group A3.

They followed that up with a chastening 4-1 defeat away to world champions Spain but were still level on points with Thomas Tuchel's Three Lions before Saturday's humiliating loss in Rijeka.

With the top two qualifying for the latter stages, Croatia had the chance to put themselves in pole position to beat England to a place in the quarter-finals.

Yet by the time Modric was substituted in the 57th minute, the home side were already 5-0 down after conceding two goals from Harry Kane and one apiece from Jude Bellingham, Anthony Gordon and Bukayo Saka.

Modric was forced to watch from the sidelines as further goals from Saka and Morgan Rogers extended England's advantage before the final whistle.

"You can lose, or play against an opponent who is better - and they are right now," added the former Spurs favourite, who helped Croatia knock England out in the qualifying stages for the 2008 Euros where they reached the quarter-finals in Bilic's first spell as manager.

"But in any case, losing like this and squandering the reputation we've built over the years is unacceptable... [it was a] catastrophic night [for Croatia]."

It does not get any easier for Croatia, who next host Spain in Split on Tuesday, and will finish their Nations League campaign with games away to England (12 November) and at home to the Czech Republic (15 November).

"We need to pull ourselves together, stay together because a new difficult game awaits us," said Modric, with Croatia third in the table, facing a battle to retain their status in the top tier of the Nations League.

"We have to show our true colours, that there is defiance and pride in us, desire, willingness, togetherness, these things cannot be lost overnight."

articles.title: South Korea football captain apologises for 'not going to military' remark after Asian Games gold
articles.summary: South Korea's Asian Games football captain Lee Gi-hyuk apologised on Sunday for saying he would not have to do military service after his team won the
articles.body: South Korea's Asian Games football captain Lee Gi-hyuk apologised on Sunday for saying he would not have to do military service after his team won the men's gold medal.South Korea beat hosts Japan 1-0 in the men's final in Toyota, near Nagoya, on Saturday to win their fourth consecutive Asian Games title.After the victory, the 26-year-old Lee, a defender who plays in the domestic K League, held up his gold medal and told reporters: "I'm not going to the military."Able-bodied South Korean men are usually required to complete between 18 months and two years of military service before turning 28. However, the government grants exemptions to Asian Games gold medallists and Olympic medallists of any colour. Those athletes instead complete only a few weeks of basic military training.Military exemptions are a sensitive issue in South Korea, and athletes usually avoid discussing them publicly.Lee later apologised for "the thoughtless remarks I made and the way I behaved after the match, things I should not have said or done, both as captain and as a player".In a statement on Instagram, he said he was "caught up in the happiness, adrenaline and excitement of the moment"."I am deeply sorry to the fans who are currently fulfilling their military duty, as well as to all those who sincerely supported us," he said."As an adult I should have thought carefully before speaking. I deeply regret having spoken so carelessly, and I will continue to reflect on my actions."I sincerely apologise to all the fans who have supported us wholeheartedly and who are doing their utmost to fulfil their military duty."Asian Games football is played by under-23 teams, although three overage players are allowed in each squad.Lee was also part of South Korea's World Cup campaign in North America, where the team were eliminated in the group stage.Golfer Tom Kim also earned a military exemption after winning gold at the Asian Games on Saturday.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ronaldo’s wife Georgina gets involved, attacks Jorge Jesus with fake Ferguson quote over how he treated her husband
articles.summary: Georgina Rodríguez defends Cristiano Ronaldo against Jorge Jesus' treatment in the Portugal national team over a controversial departure and social media fallout.
articles.body: The fallout from Cristiano Ronaldo's sudden Portugal departure has now reached his family, with Georgina Rodríguez appearing to take aim at Jorge Jesus in a social media post that was deleted shortly afterwards. The message also carried another complication, because the statement used to criticise the Portugal coach was wrongly attributed to one of the most influential figures in Ronaldo's career, Sir Alex Ferguson.Georgina Rodriguez deletes Instagram post aimed at Jorge JesusRodríguez reportedly shared the post on her Instagram story on Saturday evening, criticising Jesus over the circumstances surrounding Ronaldo's departure from the Portugal camp.The post originated from the Hispanic Sports Media page, which continues to have the material published on Instagram, although the statement itself carries no credible source attribution and has not been reported by major media outlets across several European countries.According to Portuguese outlet A Bola, Rodríguez's post used a quote that had been falsely attributed to former Manchester United manager Sir Alex Ferguson, who recruited Ronaldo for Manchester United in 2003.The false quote read: “If Jorge Jesus knew in his heart that he didn't intend to use him, then why did he call him up in the first place? To take a stand? That's not authority, that's insecurity.”Rodríguez was also reportedly said to have added her own comment above the statement, writing: “I don't know how this man can bear the name of Christ.”The report said Rodríguez deleted the post a short time later, although screenshots of the Instagram story have continued circulating.Ronaldo's departure followed Jesus leaving him unused against NorwayThe post came only days after Ronaldo walked out of the Portugal camp on Wednesday, September 30, following the team's Nations League victory over Norway.Jesus decided against bringing Ronaldo onto the pitch despite sending the forward to warm up for around 30 minutes, with the decision becoming the immediate backdrop to the controversy that followed.An emergency meeting involving Ronaldo, Jesus and Portuguese Football Federation president Pedro Proença took place after the match, but the discussions did not prevent Ronaldo from leaving the national team set-up.A report from El Chiringuito journalist Edu Aguirre, who is described as a close friend of Ronaldo, claimed that the five-time Ballon d'Or winner felt “betrayed” by the developments, while Jesus had also indicated that he would explain his position after Portugal's following match against Norway.Ronaldo confirmed his departure in a statement posted on social media, writing: “After the press conference of the national team and following a conversation with the president of the Portuguese Football Federation, I have decided to leave the national team training camp.”He added: “In time, I will tell all the Portuguese the truth about the reasons that motivated me to leave.”Jorge Jesus plays down Ronaldo dispute as family criticism growsJesus has rejected suggestions that an explosive confrontation took place between himself and Ronaldo, insisting that the situation developed from a footballing decision rather than any personal dispute.“There was no incident whatsoever,” Jesus said. “Any player - and I was a player myself - when you spend 20 or 30 minutes warming up and then don't get on, no-one is happy about that.”Jesus also explained that he had spoken to Ronaldo before the match about his role against Denmark, telling the forward that he would not start but could still enter the game later.“Afterwards, as coach, I decided not to bring him on,” Jesus added. “It's nothing to make a fuss about.”The criticism from Ronaldo's family has nevertheless continued, with his sister Elma dos Santos Aveiro also sharing her views on Instagram two days earlier.“Cristiano deserved more respect. The national team deserved better infrastructure. Portuguese journalism deserves greater competence and less speculation,” the text began.“The Portuguese don’t deserve to be the best at anything. We are envious, contemptuous and ignorant, and we deserve to return to the mediocrity that always defined us in soccer before Cristiano,” it continued before thanking Ronaldo and saying that he “deserved more”.Aveiro made clear that she agreed with the assessment by adding: “That says it all.”Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: El Murcia recupera la sonrisa y sigue intratable como local
articles.standfirst: Tras la derrota el miércoles en Navalcarnero, el cuadro de Sergi Guilló suma su tercera victoria en tres partidos en su feudo ante un Nàstic inferior
articles.summary: Tras la derrota el miércoles en Navalcarnero, el cuadro de Sergi Guilló suma su tercera victoria en tres partidos en su feudo ante un Nàstic inferior
articles.body: Se ha repuesto muy rápido el Real Murcia del varapalo de la Copa Federación con un triunfo muy importante ante el Nàstic de Tarragona. No en su mejor partido, ya que la presión alta del Nàstic de Tarragona dificultaba la salida de balón de los murcianos. Pese a ello, el dominio evidente de los locales, que están en un buen momento de forma, han hecho que, sin haber tenido efectividad, sumen el tercer triunfo seguido en casa y se afiancen en las posiciones altas de la tabla. No se encontraba muy cómodo el cuadro de Sergi Guilló durante el inicio del partido, pero, tras soportar algún que otro susto en la salida de presión, tuvo el premio del gol en el minuto 13: un gran control de Flakus sirvió para que Jorge Mier, que llegaba como un puñal en la banda derecha, pusiese un centro que fue rematado con éxito por el ariete esloveno. El delantero, de esta forma, desataba la alegría en el Enrique Roca y se quitaba todo tipo de presión, como así escenificó en la celebración, ya que llevaba sin marcar desde la primera jornada. Poco después, una brutal parada de Dani Jiménez evitaba el empate de los tarraconenses. Pese a ello, el Murcia no le perdió la cara al encuentro ni se vino abajo, y, con un juego muy pocas veces visto en la Capital del Segura, no cejaba en su empeño de aumentar la ventaja en este primer tiempo. Los granas, con el talento de Javi Moreno y Chema Núñez, y la velocidad de Jorge Mier, hacían de la banda derecha su principal amenaza y generaban ocasiones de gol, aunque sin éxito. No obstante, no todo iba a ser un camino de rosas para los locales, ya que, en los últimos compases de la primera mitad, el Nàstic iba a arrinconar al equipo pimentonero y tuvo cerca el empate en más de una ocasión. Para fortuna murcianista, el choque se iba a vestuarios con 1-0 en el marcador. Con un cambio en las filas visitantes y sin retoques por parte pimentonera daba comienzo segunda mitad que, en sus primeros compases, no iba a tener mucha actividad. Los de Guilló seguían teniendo el dominio del encuentro, pero sin tener suerte de cara a portería más allá del tanto tempranero de Flakus. La nota negativa la ponía Jorge Mier, quien, tras un golpe, tuvo que ser sustituido y abandonaba el campo renqueante. Pasaban los minutos y la angustia se apoderaba de una grada impaciente, pese al resultado, con los suyos. Un nerviosismo que se acabaría en el minuto 81 después de que Óscar Gil cabecease un córner y suyos remate acabase en el fondo de la red. Este segundo gol trajo la tranquilidad de manera definitiva a los asientos de un Enrique Roca que empezaba a poner el foco en el próximo encuentro de este miércoles a las 20.30 ante el eterno rival, el FC Cartagena, en el choque aplazado correspondiente a la jornada cinco. Bustos, m. 54), Joel Jorquera, David Flakus. Nàstic de Tarragona: Vicent Abril, Manuel Royo, Athuman, Joseda, Subirats (Gabarri, m. 66), Meshak, Montalvo, Almansa (Villote, m. 80), Carlos Segura (Marco, m.75), Joan Prohens (Borja Sánchez, m. 46), Diego Gómez (Bakiš, m. 66). Goles: 1-0 Flakus, m. 13; 2-0 Óscar Gil, m. 81. Incidencias: Partido correspondiente a la sexta jornada del Grupo II de la Primera RFEF. Asistieron 15.013 espectadores.

articles.body: Estados Unidos anunció la lista de 26 jugadoras convocadas para los dos amistosos que disputarán ante España los días 10 (20:30 horas) y 14 de octubre (1:00 hora). Entre las seleccionadas destaca el regreso de Naomi Girma y Sam Coffey; la primera vez para Trinity Byars, Pietra Tordin y Evelyn Shores; y las cuatro máximas goleadoras de la NWSL: Ashley Sanchez, Sophia Wilson, Trinity Rodman y Trinity Byars. "Si bien tenemos muchas ganas de enfrentarnos a las campeonas del mundo, siempre vuelvo al camino que estamos recorriendo juntas", aseguró Emma Hayes al dar la lista. "Esta concentración servirá para restablecer las conexiones después de un largo descanso, analizar a algunas jugadoras que no han estado con nosotras en este ciclo y ofrecer el mejor rendimiento posible ante estadios llenos. Por supuesto, nuestro objetivo secundario también será la preparación final para el torneo clasificatorio para el Mundial", añadió. articles.standfirst: La película de moda explora la intensa relación entre Federico García Lorca y Rafael Rodríguez Rapún, que defendió la camiseta del Atlético en sus categorías inferiores
articles.summary: La película de moda explora la intensa relación entre Federico García Lorca y Rafael Rodríguez Rapún, que defendió la camiseta del Atlético en sus categorías inferiores
articles.body: Rafael: “[...] Mi padre quería que fuese médico hasta que se dio cuenta de que me mareaba si veía un poco de sangre. Por eso dejé también el fútbol. Me daba pánico la sangre. Antes de todo esto. Un poco de sangre. Y ahora mira”. - Sebastián: “¿Has jugado al fútbol?” - Rafael: “Sí”. - Sebastián: “¿En qué equipo? ¿Eras conocido?” - Rafael: “¿Eras?” - Sebastián: “Es un modo de hablar”. - Rafael: “En el Atlético de Madrid. Pero nunca llegué a jugar en el primer equipo”.] ¿Cómo se llega de la película de moda y de la obra teatral en la que se basa, teniendo en cuenta las “licencias poéticas sustanciales” de ambas, al Atlético de Madrid de hace casi un siglo, teniendo en cuenta también que aquello debió durar lo justo? Pues con lo que cuenta una familia, con lo que recogen los que han trabajado sobre el tema... y con una fotografía. “Yo he visto esa foto. De hecho guardo una copia en mi despacho. Los de entonces eran equipos diferentes y las de entonces eran categorías diferentes, así que no puedo asegurar que se trate del juvenil, pero yo he visto esa foto y es el Atlético en el campo de La Guindalera, que se utilizaba por entonces. Y se trata de Rafael. No es que sea un perito, pero cierto peritaje sí tengo. De hecho también he visto su carnet de socio. Creo que lo fue hasta el final de sus días”. Se lo asegura a MARCA José Antonio Martín Otín, Petón, una de las pocas personas que, con la autoridad que confiere lo estudiado, lo investigado, lo documentado, lo escrito, puede hablar de ese Rafael, que no es otro que Rodríguez Rapún. RRR. “Todas las facetas de Rafael nacen del mismo compromiso. Era un hombre atlético, de complexión fuerte, que jugó al fútbol desde pequeño. Es decisivo el papel que el deporte tuvo en los movimientos obreros y de hecho Rafael jugó también en equipos como ‘El baluarte’, ligado a la Casa del Pueblo y la Federación Deportiva Obrera. Como dato curioso, tenía ese pánico a la sangre y yo creo que, en parte, eso le hizo no insistir mucho más en esa pasión”. Se lo describe a MARCA Alberto Conejero, una de las pocas personas que, con la autoridad que confiere lo estudiado, lo investigado, lo documentado, lo escrito, puede hablar de ese Rafael, que no es otro que Rodríguez Rapún. RRR. ‘La Bola Negra’, que causa sensación desde su estreno, que liquida las taquillas, que entre otros ha ganado el Premio a la Mejor Dirección en el Festival de Cannes o el Premio del Público en el de San Sebastián, que ha sido seleccionada por la Academia de Cine como candidata española para los Oscar, que ha sido dirigida por Javier Calvo y Javier Ambrossi, que está protagonizada entre otros por Guitarricadelafuente, Miguel Bernardeau (sensacional en el papel de Rapún), Carlos González, Milo Quifes, Lola Dueñas, Penélope Cruz o Glenn Close, es una película que enlaza historias situadas, todas alrededor del deseo, la identidad, la memoria y la herencia, en distintos momentos de los siglos XX y XXI. Y una de ellas pasa precisamente por la profunda relación de amor entre Federico García Lorca y Rafael Rodríguez Rapún. RRR. El que jugó en el Atlético. “Este equipo está lleno de cosas maravillosas, muchas de las cuales sucedieron en aquella época. Cuando ganó el Campeonato Regional de 1928, uno de los que aparece en el banquete de celebración es Rafael Alberti”, desarrolla Petón. “Y precisamente en la última fotografía de Lorca en Madrid, aparece con Rosario Bergamín, jugadora destacada del entonces Athletic Club de Madrid en hockey”, añade, convencido como está de que al gran poeta le gustaba el fútbol: “Para que contestara había que preguntárselo y resulta que lo había hecho por nosotros la revista ‘Miradero’ en 1931, aunque esa respuesta anduviera perdida 81 años hasta que la recuperó el Centro de Documentación Teatral”... [“Cuando presencio un partido, unos me son más simpáticos que otros. Conquistan espontáneamente la simpatía por cualquier accidente del juego. Y deseo que gane el que más rápidamente me captó. Voy al espectáculo deportivo sin prejuicio alguno”.] “Si me hubieran preguntado a mí hace 30 años, hubiera dicho que no le gustaba”, recupera el hilo Petón, “pero porque soy tonto: en realidad su curiosidad por las cosas hubiera impulsado a decir que sí. Y pongámonos en su lugar: tú no eres de ningún equipo pero llegas a un sitio y te enamoras de un aficionado. Vas con él y, descubriendo lo que disfruta y lo que sufre, al final compartirás esa pasión. Querrás, en definitiva, que gane ese equipo. Así que podemos entender que Lorca sentía simpatía por el Atlético. Además era muy amigo de Marcelino Galatas, que sí llegó a jugar en el primer equipo”, completa. “No sólo por Rafael”, interviene Conejero respecto al interés de Federico por el fútbol, “sino también por la influencia decisiva de su amigo José María de Cossío. Sorprende de nuevo la importancia de Santander, allí donde Rapún y Lorca estuvieron juntos, con La Barraca en un verano feliz, allí donde murió y fue enterrado Rafael. Hablo de Santander y es que Lorca fue al Metropolitano, a ver un partido de fútbol de España contra los checos, porque jugaba un futbolista del Racing que presidía entonces Cossío. La suya es una figura que debe ser reivindicada también”, añade el autor de ‘La Piedra Oscura’, obra teatral que ficciona los últimos días de Rapún y desde la que los Javis imaginaron ‘La Bola Negra’, convirtiendo de hecho a Conejero en coguionista de un largometraje que en todo caso también se basa en otros textos de Lorca. Y en cuyo éxito no resulta exagerado insistir mientras navega el segundo fin de semana en los cines, superados hace días el millón de espectadores y rondando los diez millones de recaudación. “Lo llevo con infinito agradecimiento a todos los que están llenando las salas. Muchísimos de ellos se están interesando además por el texto teatral. Aunque ya llevaba más de una decena de ediciones, está teniendo un nuevo impulso. Así que mi alegría es como guionista de la película, pero también como autor de la obra”, resume el dramaturgo. Regresando al fútbol, por cierto, otra presencia de Lorca en el antiguo estadio del Atlético que no ha llegado a confirmarse del todo es la de aquel partido ante el Sevilla en 1936 que certificó el descenso rojiblanco, toda vez que, con 2-3 en el marcador, Chacho falló un penalti que hubiera derivado en la permanencia. Pero existe, material para coleccionistas, una localidad de unos amigos suyos en la que por detrás pone ‘Para Federico’. Aquel encuentro se disputó el 19 de abril, cuatro meses antes de su muerte, pero cierto es que hasta el 13 de julio no concretaría su decisión, fatídica por las consecuencias que tuvo, de regresar desde Madrid a Granada, “huyendo de un conflicto que tenía todo aquello que no le gustaba”. Uno y otro, Conejero y Petón, tuvieron, por otra parte, la oportunidad de entrevistarse con la familia de Rafael. En el caso del primero, llegó a tiempo de hacerlo con su hermano Tomás, “quien -puede leerse en una nota del autor a su propia obra- en la primavera y el verano de Madrid de 2012, y a sus 95 años, compartió conmigo horas de recuerdos y las reliquias de aquella relación. A su generosidad, alegría y al alto vuelo de su espíritu está dedicada esta obra”; en el de ambos, colaboraron Marga y Sofía, hijas del propio Tomás y por tanto sobrinas de Rafael. “Nunca olvidaré la primera tarde que mi amigo José Manuel Tenorio y yo pasamos en su casa -apunta Petón-, o que en una segunda visita sacaran aquel álbum de fotos”. Rapún estudiaba para Ingeniero de Minas ("la cuna universitaria del Atlético desde que aquellos estudiantes lo fundaron”), fue secretario de La Barraca y, a partir del grupo ambulante de teatro, convirtiéndose además en inspiración para los conmovedores ‘Sonetos del amor oscuro’, compañero de García Lorca los últimos años de sus vidas. De hecho Rafael murió exactamente uno más tarde, maldito 18 de agosto [en su nicho aparece el 19], él en Santander malherido por un ataque aéreo en Bárcena de Pie de Concha (sus restos reposan en el cementerio de Ciriego), Federico asesinado en Granada. “Rapún fue un hombre profundamente comprometido con la Segunda República y con sus ideales socialistas, también lógicamente un apasionado de la literatura y del teatro. Es asombrosa la actividad que desplegó en su corta vida, una de las innumerables vidas de jóvenes segadas por nuestra guerra”, abunda Conejero. “Combatiente, valiente, cabezón en el buen sentido, líder en todos los sentidos...”, enumera Petón, que en el marco de sus investigaciones ha hecho un descubrimiento “espeluznante” por lo personal para el que, “la fortuna sentimental tiene importancia”, no resultan estas páginas marco adecuado. Queda aún una cuenta pendiente. Y Conejero no olvida: “La familia de Rafael siempre fue generosa conmigo. Comprendieron esas sustanciales licencias poéticas entonces y las han comprendido ahora. Ahora bien, he de cumplir mi promesa de escribir la biografía de Rapún, con literatura pero sin esas licencias”. [El diálogo ficcionado que abre este reportaje y en el que aparece el Atlético corresponde a ‘La Piedra Oscura’, en la que Alberto Conejero imagina las últimas horas del protagonista. En ‘La Bola Negra’ apenas hay una referencia directa al equipo, hecha además en tono despectivo por un alto mando del ejército franquista. Obra y película son imprescindibles y giran en torno a esa figura con biografía pendiente. Rafael Rodríguez Rapún. RRR. El que vistió la rojiblanca. Sí, el del Atleti...]

articles.title: Así vivieron los jugadores del Sporting Hortaleza el ataque a su autobús: "¿Nos lo van a dar por perdido, verdad? Qué bonito es el fútbol"
articles.summary: El partido de la previa de la Copa del Rey entre el Atlético Unión Güímar y el Sporting Hortaleza ha sido suspendido este domingo en Tasagaya, después de que el conjunto madrileño considerara que no se daban las condiciones necesarias para garantizar su seguridad. Los visitantes permanecieron durante un largo periodo en los vestuarios y se han negado inicialmente a saltar al terreno de juego, hasta la llegada de efectivos de la Guardia Civil y la Policía Nacional. El encuentro, que debía decidir qué equipo avanzaba a la primera eliminatoria de la Copa del Rey -con el aliciente de enfrentarse posteriormente a Sevilla, Betis, Rayo Vallecano o Getafe-, estaba marcado además por el 1-0 favorable al Sporting Hortaleza en la ida.

articles.title: Rugby League World Cup: Leeds Rhinos' star man Jake Connor left out of England 23-player squad
articles.summary: Jake Connor has been left out of England’s 23-player squad for the upcoming Rugby League World Cup, with Mikey Lewis expected to be selected ahead of him for the tournament in Australia, New Zealand and Papua New Guinea this October and November.
articles.body:
Connor is a surprise omission from Brian McDermott's squad for the tournament, which will be held across Australia, New Zealand and Papua New Guinea this October and November.

Last year's Man of Steel won't be making the cut once again after his Ashes snub last year, despite finishing top of Super League's assist charts with 43.

The 31-year-old was controversially omitted from Shaun Wane's squad for last autumn's home Ashes series against Australia, which England lost 3-0.

Wane stepped down earlier this year, with former Leeds head coach Brian McDermott appointed to lead England through to the end of the World Cup.

McDermott had previously defended Connor, saying in April: "I think the rhetoric and the narrative around Jake was tremendously unfair. I understand where Jake Connor comes from in that he's liked by some and disliked by others. OK, that comes in the nature of the game.

"We could sit around a table and debate whether he's a nice person or not. I just don't think that's a fair narrative to be made public and that was the rhetoric around him.

"What nobody can argue is that he's a tremendous player. He's a fantastic player. He's a game-breaker."

McDermott's full squad will be announced on Monday with Hull KR fullback Mikey Lewis expected to be be selected ahead of Connor.

England get their World Cup under way on October 17 against Tonga in Perth, with games against France and Papua New Guinea to follow.

England, runners-up in 1975, 1995 and 2017, reached the semi-finals on home soil in 2021, only to suffer a defeat by Samoa.
