articles.title: Luismi aprovecha los errores del meta del Europa para sacar al Huesca de la crisis
articles.standfirst: Un doblete suyo tras dos fallos de Nil condenaron a los catalanes
articles.summary: Un doblete suyo tras dos fallos de Nil condenaron a los catalanes
articles.body: Cinco jornadas después, el Huesca retomó el camino de la victoria. No lo hacía desde la primera jornada. Los oscenses vencieron al Europa por 3-1 en un partido cómodo que les permite colocarse a dos del playoff. Dos fallos del meta Nil Ruíz terminaron en un doblete de Luismi. En el tramo final, Cristian Herrera selló la goleada ante un cuadro catalán que seguirá en descenso. Gori anotó la única diana visitante de penalti en el descuento. Los locales salieron decididos a romper el partido pronto. Diego Gómez fue una auténtica pesadilla para la defensa rival y nada más comenzar estuvo a punto de marcar. Juárez, siempre dinámico, se topó con una gran mano de Nil y de nuevo Gómez tuvo otra de cabeza. El gol era cuestión de tiempo pero llegó de la forma más inesperada. Un grave error del meta del Europa terminó en el tanto de Luismi. Se puso a controlar en el área pequeña sin ver a su oponente que le quitó el balón para empujarla a la red. Los catalanes reaccionaron con dos llegadas peligrosas pero el partido ya estaba como querían los de Raúl Jardiel. Tanto fue así que en la última jugada de la primera mitad, otro error de Nil en un mal despeje, sería aprovechado de nuevo por Luismi. 2-0 al descanso y encuentro prácticamente decidido. En la segunda mitad, el Europa lo intentó pero no era el día. Hasta les anularon un gol de Khalid por un fuera de juego que dejó muchas dudas. El Huesca buscó el tercero sin mucha convicción, aunque lo encontró en los últimos instantes en una gran jugada de Douglas que sirvió en bandeja el tanto a Cristian Herrera. En el descuento, Salva Ruíz fue expulsado por doble amarilla y Gori maquilló el resultado de penalti. Así, los azulgranas firmaron un triunfo balsámico que da aire a su entrenador. FICHA TÉCNICA: 3-Huesca: Gazzaniga, Víctor García, Kembo, Molina, Salva Ruíz, Sielva (Douglas 84'), Jimmy (Gorostidi 61'), Diego Gómez (Iván Rodríguez 84'), Pascu, Luismi (Mario García 78') y Juárez (Cristian Herrera 61') 1-Europa: Nil Ruíz, Coto, Campeny, Cano, Edo (Mascaró 46'), Tito (Morales 73'), Gori, Teto (Cadenas 73'), Flavio, Sgró (Padillo 63') y Khalid (Youssef 73'). Goles: 1-0 Luismi 29', 2-0 Luismi 45', 3-0 Cristian Herrera 89' y 3-1 Gori de penalti 94'. Árbitro: Aimar Velasco Arbaiza (Colegio vasco). Amonestó a Edo 45', Mascaró 63', Gorostidi 65' y Sielva 80'. Expulsó a Salva Ruíz por doble amarilla 90' y 92'. Estadio: El Alcoraz con 4.318 espectadores.

articles.title: Junior confirma su lesión y señala al formato del parón de selecciones
articles.standfirst: El jugador del Betis tuvo que retirarse a los diez minutos del partido frente a Haití
articles.summary: El jugador del Betis tuvo que retirarse a los diez minutos del partido frente a Haití
articles.body: Junior Firpo se lesionó en el último encuentro internacional de República Dominicana frente a Haití. El lateral del Betis ha explicado a los medios de comunicación del país caribeño que "venía con molestias del partido contra Trinidad y Tobago y sentí un pequeño estiramiento más fuerte de la cuenta. A esperar las pruebas, a ver si regreso al club. Ya me llamaron y quieren ver qué hay". El jugador señala como 'culpable' al nuevo formato del parón de selecciones que obliga a parar las competiciones de clubes durante prácticamente tres semanas y condensa los partidos de las selecciones. "Seguro que sí". "No entendí muy bien por qué cambiaron el parón. Antes jugábamos dos partidos en diez días y era mejor que hacer cuatro en once. Ellos sabrán", comentó. Sobre si estaría ante Nicaragua dijo que "si no pude jugar el anterior partido, no creo que será posible". Con la friolera de ocho partidos en 29 días, Manuel Pellegrini, fiel a su política de rotaciones, necesita al menos dos jugadores por puesto. Fran García, otro lateral zurdo de la plantilla verdiblanca, fue convocado por Luis de la Fuente y ayer sumó noventa minutos más en sus piernas en el partido ante la República Checa. El siempre temido virus FIFA se ceba con el costado zurdo de la defensa del Betis.

articles.title: Scotland: 'Promising start' or 'shocking' display in North Macedonia?
articles.summary: The Tartan Army have given a mixed reaction to Scotland's 2-0 win away to North Macedonia in the Nations League.
articles.body:
After a tale of two halves in drawing with Slovenia followed by the false start in defeat at home to Switzerland, Sebastien Pocognoli finally got his reign as Scotland head coach off and running against North Macedonia.

A fine finish from Kieron Bowie followed by a John McGinn penalty were enough to secure a win that gives the Belgian's side some renewed hope of topping Nations League group B1, or at least finishing second.

But how did the Tartan Army react to the performance and result? Well, judging from the reaction to our call for your comments, feelings are somewhat mixed.

Bowie seizing Scotland shot after World Cup disappointment

Two going on four, five or six on good night for new Scotland era

Scotland beat North Macedonia in Nations League for Pocognoli's first win

'Refreshing' tactics in 'complete performance'

Brian: Can we please all get behind the manager and the team? So refreshing to see high pressing attacking football for a change. Was it perfect? No, but it is a start. A lot of new untested strikers at this level. At least we are making openings and being on the front foot, instead of [Steve] Clarke's let's not lose policy.

John: A complete performance from Scotland. If this is how we are to set up for future games then there will be exciting games ahead. Don't think I remember any past match we were so often on the front foot... 25 shots? Unheard of. [Scott] McKenna did lunge in, but the guy made an absolute meal of it. Worthy of a yellow, but no way was it red.

Graham: McKenna had every right to go for that ball. Very unlucky. It's a win. No genuine fan cares about the performance. The scoreline is all that matters.

Scott: Scotland win away from home and still people are moaning. Any win away from home is decent. Performance on the whole was pretty good.

Terry: Great performance. Backline set the standard. [Stephen] Welsh and [Luis] Binks look really comfortable, which let those in front structure stuff.

Stuart: Should have been more than two goals, but we've played better and lost, so I'll take the result. Beat Slovenia on Tuesday and we have a three-point lead over them and the head-to-head sewn up.

Mango: Super Bowie was fantastic and deserves man of the match. He was tenacious and tried to get in behind the defence at any cost. He scored a great solo goal to get the team's momentum going. His pace and work rate are pivotal to his game and long may it continue.

Neil: Thoroughly deserved win. Lots of good performances on the pitch, but man of the match has to be the referee. Calm and composed. Best one I've seen in a while.

Matt: This is as comfortable as I've seen Scotland away from home in a long time. Impressed with the response to the Switzerland disappointment. Hopefully Pocognoli finally bins McKenna after that ridiculous challenge. Play like this against Slovenia and we will skelp them.

Gerry: A promising start for the new manager who thankfully has selected some younger and less experienced players. Breath of fresh air compared to the previous old stale cautious management approach. I know [Andy] Robertson has been applauded, but he still makes errors. His poor pass led to McKenna's sending off and he fades against better opposition. Well done to Bowie and Welsh. McBurnie, unfortunately, as seen in the past, is not the answer to our lack of a decent striker. We never seem to get many chances to score. We did last night but failed to take them against poor opposition. Interesting to see how we deal with Slovenia at home.

Aaran: A weird game. North Macedonia decided to park the bus and it is difficult with the players Scotland have currently to dismantle a team when they do that. That being said, when they did, they found a goalkeeper who was about the only Macedonian player on the pitch who looked like he was up for it. The ref then made two bad VAR calls, the first one is a penalty, the second is a foul from McKenna on the defender. Gives as good as he got but still a foul. They balance each other out and McGinn still finds himself on the scoresheet. Would've liked to have seen more goals, but we'll take it.

Stewart: Great win. Loved the performance. However, the amount of chances the players missed is frustrating. Wee bit more composure in front on goal is needed. Every player worked really hard for the team.

Lack of cutting edge against 'poor team'

Graham: Let's not get carried away here. They were awful yet we could only score twice and managed to end up with 10 men. Our lack of quality in the final third really showed.

William: The reality is North Macedonia were utter rubbish and yet, for all our play, we managed one goal, not withstanding a penalty. If we can't put three past a team like that, and then a penalty bonus, then it's still poor.

Stuart: Totally dominant, yes, but a poor team against a very poor team. Would love to say the future is bright - here is hoping - but don't hold your breath.

Jason: I have never seen a team who constantly put pressure on themselves. Should have scored at least five goals, but slackness causes a red card and then under pressure with 10 men for the last 10 minutes. This can't keep happening. They need to wake up or we won't even qualify for our own Euro tournament.

Russell: I am sorry, but there is a lack of skilled intelligent football yet from Scotland and, to be straight, I have a funny feeling the Belgian might not be the right man.

Haz: I hope "Captain Fantastic" Robertson apologises profusely to his teammates after the game. Butchered several attacking situations in the first half trying to make it all about him, then sold poor McKenna down the river with the most inept defensive pass imaginable.

Andy: Scotland has just beaten North Macedonia and it's all "what a great result", etc, You should think how far you have fallen. Where are your upcoming Dalglish, Souness, McGrain, Jordan, Strachan, McCoist, Nicolas, Hanson, McAllister and so many great fantastic players? Where are the new upcoming players? I'm English but miss your great players and great Scottish team.

Iain: Scotland as always their own worst enemy. Should have been out of sight before the second goal from the penalty spot. Sending off was caused by a sloppy pass in defence and was totally avoidable. Another frustrating night, but a much-needed win.

Miller: Lots of domination but absolutely shocking goalscoring record.

Gerry: This Scotland team beats buying Horlicks. I honestly wouldn't go to my front window if they were playing on my lawn.

Lindsey: Let's be honest, North Macedonia are currently a poor side and we should have bagged more goals. To have that many opportunities and only get one in the net (in play) is not good enough. Tuesday night is huge. We won't be controlling the game and will therefore have to ensure better deliveries into the box so the strikers can do their job.

Maurice: How the commentators got excited about this I'll never know. Robertson and [Ben] Gannon-Doak run up and down the lines, but there is absolutely no end product. And I hope McKenna shakes Robertson's hand for the short pass that got him a red card. And [Oli] McBurnie, well, he tries!

Jeffrey: [Scott] McKenna far too rash. Yes, it's a bad pass, but an accident waiting to happen. Welsh and Binks look good and I'd give [Luke] Graham a chance. Should've been four up before the red.

Jim: I cannot get excited by this victory and would argue this was a victory that flattered us. This was a very poor North Macedonian team. We scored a terrific goal, the other being an extremely doubtful penalty. We seemingly have few striking options currently and are missing the likes of [Scott] McTominay, but it cannot disguise the scant resources available to the new manager. We need a very urgent rethink and rebuild of the game here in Scotland or we will continue to be what we currently are the "nearly boys of world football".

John: Yes a win. Performance shocking! Gannon-Doak was ponderous, slowed the movement on most occasions and his delivery, end product was dreadful. Yes, he has talent, but unless someone coaches him and works on delivery, he will be ruined. At present, he is not good enough for a national team because of these failings. John McGinn again was poor. Slow, rotten touch, not running for the team but falls down repeatedly, once or twice very embarrassingly! Mr 100 cap started strongly, but had he played a couple of passes, when required, McBurnie would have had a few goals. McBurnie again was very good. Most of his first touches opened up excellent field positions promoting a fast transition to attack. Looks very promising with Bowie. Gunn, Hendry, McKenna, McGinn, Christie have had their day.

Fergus: An okay performance against a weak team. I'm not buying it was exciting/attacking yada yada, because against a team that bad you can't gauge it. Superb performances from several. I thought Bowie was superb and never gave up. Against anyone marginally better, Scotland will get found out pretty quickly. Could do with playing consistently better opposition to see where we really are.

Neil: Scotland, in spite of dominating, were unable to put the ball in the net. Bowie scored a good goal, the penalty was soft, other than that they failed to score. Against better opposition this continued failure will be costly.

Douglas: Wow, they have won a game against a useless team. Hang the bunting out, decree a Scottish holiday - pathetic standards.

articles.title: El Barça domina Europa a ritmo de gol
articles.standfirst: Los culés, el equipo con mejor porcentaje realizador de las grandes ligas
articles.summary: Los culés, el equipo con mejor porcentaje realizador de las grandes ligas
articles.body: El arranque de temporada del Barcelona a nivel goleador está siendo espectacular y las estadísticas lo refrendan. El conjunto azulgrana se ha convertido en el equipo más goleador de las grandes ligas europeas en este inicio de curso y presenta una media anotadora difícil de igualar. Los 31 tantos marcados en las siete primeras jornadas de LaLiga sitúan al equipo de Hansi Flick en 4,4 goles por partido, un registro que ningún otro equipo de los principales campeonatos alcanza. Ni Inglaterra, ni Francia, ni Italia, ni Alemania, ni Portugal presentan, hasta el momento, unas cifras similares. El Barça domina con claridad esta clasificación y ha encontrado en el gol una de sus principales señas de identidad en este inicio de temporada. En España, la distancia respecto a sus principales rivales también resulta significativa. El Barcelona suma 31 goles en siete encuentros, con una media de 4,4 por partido. El Real Madrid, segundo en este apartado, acumula 18 tantos, lo que supone 2,5 por encuentro. El Atlético de Madrid completa el podio goleador de LaLiga con una media de 2,2 goles por cruce. La diferencia es considerable: el Barcelona está marcando casi dos goles más por encuentro que el Real Madrid y más del doble que el Atlético. Un dato que refleja la extraordinaria producción ofensiva del equipo azulgrana en estas primeras jornadas. Si se amplía la mirada al resto de las grandes ligas europeas, el Bayern de Múnich es uno de los equipos que más se acerca a los registros del Barcelona, aunque se queda lejos. El conjunto alemán ha marcado 14 goles en las cuatro jornadas disputadas de la Bundesliga, con una media de 3,5 tantos por partido. La diferencia con el Barça continúa siendo notable. Los azulgranas superan en casi un gol por encuentro al gigante alemán. En la Premier League, el equipo que presenta una mejor media goleadora en este inicio es el Brighton. El conjunto inglés ha anotado 16 goles en cinco partidos, a una media de 3,2 por encuentro. Un registro destacado, pero todavía por debajo de los 4,4 del Barcelona. En Portugal, donde hasta el momento se han disputado las mismas jornadas que en España, el Benfica suma 22 goles, nueve menos que el Barcelona. Su producción ofensiva también es notable, aunque no alcanza las cifras del conjunto azulgrana. En Italia, el Inter de Milán presenta una media de 3 goles por partido, mientras que en Francia los mejores registros se sitúan alrededor de los 2, con el Olympique de Lyon y el Strasbourg como equipos destacados en este apartado. Los números, por tanto, dibujan un escenario muy claro: el Barcelona ha comenzado la temporada a un ritmo goleador extraordinario y lidera con claridad la producción ofensiva entre los principales campeonatos europeos. Los 31 goles en siete jornadas no solo explican buena parte de su espectacular inicio, sino que también sitúan al equipo de Flick en una dimensión goleadora muy superior a la de sus principales competidores.

articles.title: Bianconere suffer late defeat in Milan
articles.summary: The Women's First Team suffered a late defeat against AC Milan on Serie A Women Matchday 2, with the Rossonere winning 2-1.Juventus took the lead at the Cent...
articles.body:
The Women's First Team suffered a late defeat against AC Milan on Serie A Women Matchday 2, with the Rossonere winning 2-1.

Juventus took the lead at the Centro Vismara through Martina Lenzini, but late goals from Thea Kyvag and Monica Renzotti saw the points stay in Lombardy.

It was Milan who created the first chance after six minutes, when Mawa Sesay had an effort on goal only to be denied by Larissa Rusek. The Rossonere tried again in the 14th minute through Ewelina Kamczyk, whose volley from the edge of the box went just wide.

Juventus responded three minutes later through Emma Stolen Godo, who fired a left-footed shot towards goal but failed to trouble Sandra Estevez. In the 20th minute, Milan came close again as Sara Stokic capitalised on a Juventus error and shot, but Rusek intercepted and saved.

In the 32nd minute, Juve began to grow into the game. Remina Chiba tried her luck from the right and Estevez tipped the ball away for a corner. From the resulting corner, it was Stolen Godo who once again tested the Rossonere goalkeeper. Before half-time, there was also a chance for Sara Kanutte Fornes, whose header went over the bar. The teams went into the dressing rooms with the score at 0–0.

JUVE COME CLOSE TO SCORING, THEN LENZINI

Juventus started the second half strongly and created a great chance in the 50th minute. Eva Schatzer played in Alba Redondo, whose left-footed shot struck the inside of the post. Amaiur Sarriegi pounced on the ball, but Nadine Sorelli cleared it off the line. Play was then halted for offside, a decision confirmed following a VAR review.

Milan's response was immediate. Christy Grimshaw tested Rusek and, in the ensuing move, Marta Mascarello hit the post. In the 60th minute, Stolen Godo tried her luck with a header, but sent the ball over the bar.

The Bianconere continued to press for the lead and, in the 71st minute, Sarriegi posed a threat on two occasions in the same move, without finding the net.

The goal finally came in the 80th minute. Sarriegi picked out Redondo, who tried to take on a defender before laying the ball off to Martina Lenzini. The captain fired home the winning goal to put Juventus ahead.

Just when Juventus seemed to have the game under control, Milan turned it around in the space of a few minutes. In the 86th minute, Kyvag launched a counter-attack and, facing Rusek, scored to make it 1-1.

Barely two minutes later, the Rossonere took the lead. Renzotti aimed for goal with a curling shot, Cecilia Salvai deflected the ball with her head, and it ended up beyond Rusek and the score was 2-1.

Juventus tried to fight back during the eight minutes of added time and, in the 95th minute, had a good chance through Sarriegi, who, from a promising position, sent the ball over the bar.

When the final whistle blew, it was Milan who were celebrating. The match ended 2–1 at the Vismara, with Juventus suffering a late comeback defeat.
